explanation: Gabriela Mistral was the pen name of Lucila Godoy Alcayaga, a schoolteacher. Pablo Neruda followed her as Chile's second literature laureate, in 1971.

claims.text: In 1945 Gabriela Mistral of Chile became the first Latin American writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Pablo Neruda won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971 and Octavio Paz, who was Mexican, in 1990; César Vallejo, who was Peruvian, never won it.
Gabriela Mistral was the pen name of Lucila Godoy Alcayaga, who worked as a schoolteacher.
Pablo Neruda, also Chilean, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971, the second Chilean to do so.
